extra.message: Weak Hardcoded Flask Secret Key — Attacker can forge arbitrary Flask session cookies, impersonate any user (including admin), and bypass CSRF tokens for state-changing actions. [verified: The SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'secure-secret-key-12345' in app.py line 25, which is easily guessable. This enables forging Flask session cookies and predicting CSRF tokens, leading to session hijacking and privilege escalation.]

Hardcoded Default Admin Credentials — Attacker can log in as admin, view all user data, progress, flags, and perform any administrative action. [verified: Default admin credentials ('admin':'password') are hardcoded in database.py:96-97 and stored in the users table. The login endpoint accepts untrusted user input (username/password) and authenticates against these credentials, allowing any attacker to log in as admin and access all administrative functionality and data.]
